records.region: Southwestern Oregon; upper Middle Fork Coquille, Myrtle Point fork joins and lower Coquille estuary
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative receiving-system identity across the selected Middle Fork Coquille, short South Fork Coquille reach and lower Coquille River. Distinct fork names remain component names, not aliases or a single scalar name imposed on every reach.
records.completion_scope: Four newly acquired USGSTopo originals establish the chosen Middle Fork opening, Camas Valley and canyon, Middle/South/North fork joining sequence around Myrtle Point, receiving Coquille corridor and actual Bandon entrance-estuary ending. Independent Coquille Watershed Association prose corroborates the receiving system and outlet. Coquille River is supported as the representative identity; no scalar or accepted name is applied.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative receiving-system identity across the selected Middle Fork Coquille, short South Fork Coquille reach and lower Coquille River. Distinct fork names remain component names, not aliases or a single scalar name imposed on every reach.

scope_limits: Coquille River is the receiving-system identity; Middle Fork Coquille River and South Fork Coquille River are separately named component reaches, and North Fork is an unselected joining branch.

Kinnan Reservoir and the lower river’s log-pond/reservoir settings are observed in relation to the connected river corridor. The generalized selection is not assigned a precise reservoir, gate, canal or operational passage.

The selected terminal is the connected entrance-estuary water beside Bandon. The source endpoint and rendered ending are distinct; neither requires a farther selected extension into the offshore ocean.
The selected positions simplify meanders and some floodplain bends. No exact channel-bank, name-change vertex or present wetted thread is asserted.
Formal naming registry and contemporary flow or managed-operation status remain unverified.

records.region: Southeast Greenland, inland ice and the glaciated bedrock coast northwest of the original’s Skjoldungen / Sagisikuik regional label.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The original covers the full inland-ice to ice/nunatak/bedrock to inner coastal setting, but identifies neither a representative named natural river nor continuous river hydraulics along the selected object.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The single mainstem opens inland, descends south-southeast on ice, turns east through the nunatak and exposed-rock belt, and bends southeast toward the actual ending in the inner coastal setting. No tributary fragments are supplied.
records.completion_scope: All parts, roles, stages, internal joins and the actual ending are covered by the inspected original at ordinary geographic scale. Completion is of terrain correspondence; it does not require or assert exact modern banks, hydraulic links or named glacier/fjord assignment.
records.supported_name_scope: No representative or whole-route natural-river hydronym established.

scope_limits: Natural-river identity and surface or subglacial hydraulic continuity remain unestablished.
The national original depicts mixed ice and exposed bedrock rather than one surveyed river along the model line.
The actual ending has complete ordinary geographic setting coverage, but its precise relationship to the historical or modern shoreline/ice front is not established.
No exact glacier or receiving-fjord identity is assigned from neighboring labels.
The national scale does not resolve minor meltwater channels, small lakes, exact banks or transition vertices; no named lake/reservoir/managed passage is positively established.
Formal registry status and unnamed local feature names remain unverified.

bounded_name_observations.role: Wider original-map orientation southeast of the selected terminal setting; not a river, glacier or receiving-fjord assignment.

records.region: Southern Lago de Maracaibo lowlands, Escalante collector and Santa Bárbara–San Carlos del Zulia corridor
records.material_pending_reason: The chosen southwestern opening crosses a cultivated, wet and partly wooded drainage plain with several distinct channels and drains. The regional map and the historical field-study sketch do not establish the selected opening's particular through-link into the first clearly joined Escalante collector; imagery also leaves that network choice unresolved. This is a missing ordinary-scale source connection, not a demand for exact banks, perennial flow or present hydraulic operation.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The named Escalante lowland collector, selected eastern Santa Bárbara–San Carlos passage and lakeward river. The southwestern selected opening and its through-connection are not assigned this name solely from basin membership.
records.completion_scope: One bounded pass examined the one stage3 mainstem fragment, all30 stored parts, selected southwestern opening, intermediate joins, eastern town-side/managed setting, wetland approach and actual lake ending. The Escalante middle/lower correspondence is supported, but one opening-to-collector through-link remains material pending. No competing completed/scope-hold status is assigned.
records.supported_name_scope: The named Escalante lowland collector, selected eastern Santa Bárbara–San Carlos passage and lakeward river. The southwestern selected opening and its through-connection are not assigned this name solely from basin membership.

scope_limits: Río Escalante is supported for the middle/lower named corridor; it remains only a provisional representative-system candidate until the chosen opening's through-link is established.
The upper lowland contains diffuse, abandoned and managed drainage. Regional basin membership and nearby named rivers cannot substitute for the selected feeder connection.
The selected town-side reach is geographically distinct from the western channel/dike route. No diversion name, construction chronology or operating state is assigned from search discovery alone.
The model's sea terminal metadata is preserved unchanged, but the observed receiver is Lago de Maracaibo.

Historical preliminary field interpretation and current undated imagery are used at ordinary corridor scale; neither establishes an exact spring, named vertex, formal registry entry or current engineering state.

bounded_name_observations.role: Supported middle/lower corridor; opening connection remains material pending.

bounded_name_observations.role: Actual receiving lake, not a river alias or open-sea ending.

records.region: Sinaloa: upper Évora valley, Mocorito, Presa Eustaquio Buelna, Guamúchil, Angostura and the northeastern Santa María coastal receiving margin.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity supported by direct Évora inscriptions on the connected upper, reservoir-outlet and lower river. Presa Eustaquio Buelna remains a distinct selected waterbody. The name is not imposed as a scalar name on the reservoir, all irrigation canals or every coastal ditch. Mocorito is retained as a locality and published basin name, not asserted here as a verified river-name alias.
records.completion_scope: Ordinary historical mapped and photographic correspondence covers the chosen headward opening, all selected parts and joins, Eustaquio Buelna entry and outlet, the managed agricultural plain, the embanked coastal approach and the actual Santa María receiving terminal. It establishes a river-system corridor rather than exact banks, uninterrupted current surface flow, a particular operating route through control structures or a formal source/mouth coordinate.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity supported by direct Évora inscriptions on the connected upper, reservoir-outlet and lower river. Presa Eustaquio Buelna remains a distinct selected waterbody. The name is not imposed as a scalar name on the reservoir, all irrigation canals or every coastal ditch. Mocorito is retained as a locality and published basin name, not asserted here as a verified river-name alias.

scope_limits: Formal registry status, exact source and mouth coordinates, and legally fixed name boundaries remain unverified.
Mocorito occurs as a locality and basin name in the inspected originals; no river-alias equivalence is inferred from those uses alone.

The selected reservoir and lower coastal plain are managed or modified. The completed geographic correspondence does not imply a free-flowing natural river throughout or establish present control-structure operation.
Historical mapping and imagery with unverified mosaic dates do not establish current water extent, perennial discharge or an individual presently wetted coastal branch.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
